subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Sahrawi Tea: Ceremony in the Desert
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Sahrawi Tea: Ceremony in the Desert.

hook.text: In the Western Sahara, nomadic Sahrawi people prepare tea in a ritual that can take over an hour on sand and coals.

buildup.text: Green tea is boiled with a mountain of sugar in a small metal pot, then poured back and forth to create foam.

discovery.text: Three rounds are served with decreasing sugar: the first is sweet, the second moderate, the third barely sweetened.

twist.text: The ceremony happens in desert heat—yet hot tea cools the body by triggering sweat more than cold drinks do.

climax.text: For Sahrawi nomads, the tea ceremony is the social glue that holds communities together across vast, empty landscapes.

punchline.text: Sand, coals, sugar, and hospitality. In the desert, tea is home.

quiz.question: Why does hot tea actually cool the body in desert heat?
options: It triggers sweating that cools the body more effectively than cold drinks

details.summary: The Sahrawi people of the Western Sahara practice a tea ceremony using Chinese gunpowder green tea, mint, and huge amounts of sugar. Three rounds are served, each with different characteristics. The ceremony is the social heart of Sahrawi life, performed multiple times daily in desert camps.
details.whyItMatters: Sahrawi tea culture transforms a basic commodity into the primary social ritual of a desert-dwelling people, showing tea's adaptability to the most extreme environments.
takeaways: Sahrawi tea uses gunpowder green tea, mint, and abundant sugar
Three rounds are served with progressively different character
The ceremony is central to social life in desert communities

faq.question: What do the three rounds of Sahrawi tea represent?
faq.answer: Like Moroccan tea, the three rounds carry symbolic meaning. The first is bitter as life, the second sweet as love, the third gentle as death. In practice, the tea gets progressively weaker and sweeter as the leaves are reused and more sugar is added with each round.

faq.question: Why is tea so important to the Sahrawi people?
faq.answer: In the harsh desert environment, tea is the primary social activity. It structures the day, provides hydration and energy, offers hospitality to visitors, and creates space for conversation and community. For displaced Sahrawis in refugee camps, the tea ceremony maintains cultural identity.
